01_recipe_editor.png:
This is the Recipe Editor landing/overview page ("enter_recipe_editor") of an OV80i AI Vision System, reached from the All Recipes page by opening the editor for the active recipe. The left navigation lists All Recipes, Recipe Editor (highlighted/selected), Recipe Backtesting, HMI, Library, Haystack, Industrial Ethernet, I/O Live Monitor, Users and Permissions, Tools, Diagnostic Logs, System Settings, and Software Update at the bottom. The top bar shows a green "Recipe Active" pill, Version: v2026.6.0-OV80i and Serial: gsac177082, plus theme and user icons. The header reads "#4 Camera 56959 Tail" with a pencil rename icon, "PLC Recipe ID: 7", and the description "Description for Recipe 1 (imported 4x)". A recipe selector dropdown showing "#4 Camera 56959 Tail" and an "Export" button sit at the top right.

The page presents the whole configuration pipeline as cards. The Imaging Setup card (left) shows the current template/last capture: a brightly lit metal automotive stamped part — an elongated, curved sheet-metal rail/bracket with a row of round punched holes along its flange — resting on a dark, oily/grimy fixture with rusty metalwork visible; a warm orange glow appears at the bottom edge. Settings listed: Trigger Settings: PLC Trigger Mode (the plant PLC triggers each in-line cycle), Exposure (ms): 20ms, Gain: 1, Gamma: 30, with a "Configure Imaging" link. No photometric stereo, HDR, rotation, interval trigger or strobe indicators are shown.

The middle "Image Alignment & Inspection Setup" card offers "Template Image and Alignment" (tracks object orientation regardless of position or rotation) and "Inspection Parameters" (define parts of the image to focus on and make decisions). The "AI Blocks" card shows Classification (2 Models) and Segmentation (1 Model) as active, while OCR (0 Models), Measurement (0 Models) and Unsupervised (0 Models) are greyed out; a purple "Train Models" button is present. The right column has "Set Pass/Fail & IO Logic" with the text "Configure IO and Node-RED integrations here." and a "Configure IO" link; "Remote Storage" marked "Disabled" with a "Configure Remote Storage" link; and a prominent "Deploy Recipe" button. A help "?" bubble floats bottom-right.

Intent: an in-line, PLC-triggered inspection of a tail-end sheet-metal rail part combining two classification models (per-ROI class decisions) with one pixel-level segmentation model for defect masks. No individual ROI names, class names, counts, training metrics or capture navigation are exposed on this overview screen, and no banners, warnings or modals are open.

04_roi_horn-quality.png:
This is the Inspection Setup screen ("Inspection Editor") of the OV80i AI Vision System web UI, reached from the recipe tab bar for recipe "#4 Camera 56959 Tail". It sits in the middle of the recipe pipeline: after Imaging Setup and Template Image and Alignment, and before the per-model AI blocks (Classification Block, Segmentation Block, Measurement Block, OCR Block, Unsupervised Block), Train and IO Logic — all of which are visible as tabs across the top. Its stated role is given in the subtitle: "Use it to define parts of the image that you want to focus on and make decisions." The top bar shows a "Recipe Inactive" pill (this recipe is not the one currently running), Version v2026.6.0-OV80i and Serial gsac177082, plus theme and user icons. The left navigation lists All Recipes (highlighted), Recipe Editor, Recipe Backtesting, HMI, Library, Haystack, Industrial Ethernet, I/O Live Monitor, Users and Permissions, Tools, Diagnostic Logs, System Settings and Software Update.

The Inspection Setup panel lists three models: "Horn Qua..." (badge C, Classification, currently selected), "Cracks" (badge S, Segmentation) and "Hole Pres..." (badge C, Classification), with an "Add" dropdown and a settings gear beneath, and an unchecked "Live Preview Mode" checkbox. The detail pane for the selected model "Horn Quality" shows a "Classification" chip, buttons "Add Inspection Type" and "Ignore Template Region", and one expanded inspection type card titled "Missing End" reading "1 ROI • 2 Classes" with edit and delete icons. Its tabs read "ROIs (1)" and "Classes (2)"; the ROIs tab is active, showing "Region of Interest", an "Add ROI" link, a "Search ROIs" box and a single draggable ROI entry named "Horn" with edit/delete icons.

The canvas shows a live-lit color capture of a long, curved, bright galvanized stamped rail/tail bracket held in a brass-and-steel fixture with oily, speckled surroundings. Overlays are on ("Bounding Boxes" and "ROI Labels" toggles both enabled; Reset, zoom-out and zoom-in buttons above). Magenta rotated boxes labeled C1–C5 tile the length of the rail (crack-segmentation regions) and small magenta boxes H1–H6 sit on individual holes (hole-presence regions), while the selected model's ROI is drawn in yellow at the right end labeled "Horn", enclosing the flared end of the part. A geometry bar below offers H, W, X, Y all "0", angle "0°", Align and Dist alignment tools and an undo button, with hints about Shift+drag multi-select, right-click context menu, and Del/Backspace to remove ROIs. Intent: inspect a formed tail rail for cracks (pixel-level segmentation along the body), hole presence at six locations, and horn quality — specifically a "Missing End" two-class decision on the horn region.

Its controls are: "Filter By ROI :" with an empty dropdown showing placeholder "Filter by ROI"; "Visualization Mode :" set to "Default"; an "Opacity :" slider with the handle a little past the mid-left position; and a zoom control at right (magnifier-minus icon, slider with handle roughly two-thirds along, magnifier-plus icon). Several first-row crops carry bright yellow segmentation brush strokes: thin curved or elongated streaks adjacent to a round hole, one notably long thick yellow stroke, indicating labelled linear defects (scratch/crack/burr-type flaws) near hole edges. Second- and third-row tiles are unannotated (good/clean examples). Lighting is even but the parts appear slightly dark with specular highlights. No warnings, banners, accuracy metrics, exposure/gain/trigger values or recipe status pills are visible.
